23.5.2 Complexity Indicators
Consider these factors when determining complexity:
Component Count: - toy: 1-3 components - small: 3-10 components - medium: 10-30 components - large: 30+ components
Interface Count: - toy: 1-3 interfaces - small: 3-10 interfaces - medium: 10-30 interfaces - large: 30+ interfaces
Workflow Complexity: - toy: 1-2 simple workflows - small: 3-5 workflows with some branching - medium: 5-15 workflows with error handling - large: 15+ workflows with complex orchestration
Team Requirements: - toy: Single developer can build and maintain - small: Small team, limited specialization - medium: Multiple teams with clear boundaries - large: Multiple teams with extensive coordination


23.5.3 Complexity Adjustment
If a system spans multiple dimensions (e.g., many components but simple workflows), use the dominant dimension to determine complexity.
Example: A data pipeline with 20 components but only 2 sequential stages might be classified as medium rather than large because workflow complexity is low.

Category

24.9.3 Common Pitfalls

24.10 Review Process Guidelines

24.10.1 Pre-Review Preparation

Understand Context: Review any supporting documentation or requirements
Set Review Criteria: Determine which checklist items apply based on system type and complexity
Allocate Time: Complex blueprints may require 30-60 minutes for thorough review



24.10.2 Review Execution

Completeness Check: Verify all 6 kernel sections are present (Dimension 1)
Consistency Check: Validate all references are correct (Dimension 2)
Detailed Review: Go through Dimensions 3-7 systematically
Document Findings: Record all issues with severity indicators
Categorize Outcome: Determine Approved, Revision Required, or Rejected



24.10.3 Issue Documentation Template
For each issue found, document:
Issue ID: [unique identifier]
Dimension: [1-7]
Severity: [🔴 Critical / 🟡 Important / 🟢 Advisory]
Finding: [Description of issue]
Location: [Specific section or line]
Impact: [Why this matters]
Recommended Action: [How to fix]


24.10.4 Review Communication
For Approved Blueprints: - Acknowledge approval - Note any advisory items for future improvement - Confirm repository storage location
For Revision Required: - List all critical and important issues - Provide specific guidance for fixes - Set timeline for resubmission - Offer clarification if needed
For Rejected Blueprints: - Explain why blueprint cannot be salvaged - Suggest redesign approach - Provide resources for improvement - Encourage resubmission after major revisions

title: 24  Appendix C — Blueprint Review Checklist
text:
24.11 Example Review

24.11.1 Blueprint Summary
Blueprint ID: com.taskmanager.webapp.v1 System Type: Web Application Complexity: medium Review Date: 2026-03-11 Reviewer: Architecture Review Team


24.11.2 Review Findings

24.11.2.1 Critical Issues (🔴) - Must Fix
C-1: Undefined Component Reference - Dimension: 2 (Structural Consistency) - Location: Workflow workflow.create_task, step create_task_record - Finding: References component.task_orchestrator which is not defined in components: list - Impact: Workflow cannot be executed; blueprint structurally invalid - Action: Add missing component or correct reference to existing component
C-2: Missing External System Boundary - Dimension: 6 (Composability) - Location: Component component.email_provider - Finding: External SendGrid service not marked with external: true - Impact: System boundary unclear; affects integration planning - Action: Add external: true and document external dependency


24.11.2.2 Important Issues (🟡) - Should Fix
I-1: Workflow Missing Error Handling - Dimension: 5 (Operational Behavior) - Location: All workflows - Finding: No error_handling: sections defined for any workflows - Impact: Operational planning incomplete; failure modes unclear - Action: Add error handling to at least critical workflows (user login, task creation)
I-2: Interface Protocol Vague - Dimension: 3 (Interface Clarity) - Location: Interface interface.user_api - Finding: Protocol specified as REST without HTTP details - Impact: Integration ambiguity; protocol specifics unclear - Action: Specify as HTTP/REST with details (e.g., authentication, rate limiting)
I-3: Success Metrics Missing - Dimension: 1 (Structural Completeness) - Location: Goal section - Finding: Goal has no success_metrics: defined - Impact: System success criteria undefined - Action: Add measurable success metrics (e.g., response time, throughput)


24.11.2.3 Advisory Items (🟢) - Nice to Have
A-1: Data Retention Policy - Dimension: 4 (Data Ownership and Flow) - Location: Data entities - Finding: No retention policies specified for any data entities - Impact: Compliance planning incomplete - Action: Consider adding retention policies for audit logs and user data
A-2: Complexity May Be Underrated - Dimension: 7 (Feasibility) - Location: Blueprint metadata - Finding: Labeled as complexity: medium but 18 components suggests large - Impact: May underestimate implementation effort - Action: Consider reclassifying as complexity: large



24.11.3 Review Outcome
Status: Revision Required
Rationale: Blueprint has structural consistency issues (undefined components) and missing critical documentation (error handling, success metrics). These issues must be addressed before approval.
Action Items: 1. Fix undefined component reference (C-1) 2. Mark external dependency correctly (C-2) 3. Add error handling to critical workflows (I-1) 4. Clarify interface protocols (I-2) 5. Define success metrics (I-1)
Timeline: Resubmit within 5 business days


24.11.4 Approval Criteria
Blueprint will be approved when: - All critical issues (C-1, C-2) are resolved - At least critical workflows have error handling defined - Success metrics are documented - Interface protocols are clarified

25.1.2 YAML Structure
---
blueprint:
  id: cli.todo.manager.v1
  name: CLI Todo Manager
  version: 1.0.0
  system_type: CLI Tool
  complexity: small
  created_date: 2026-03-11
  authors: [Command Line Tools Team]

goal:
  description: |
    Provide a simple, efficient command-line interface for managing personal task lists.
    Enable users to create, organize, and track tasks with minimal friction.
  success_metrics:
    - metric: "Command execution time"
      target: "< 100ms (p95)"
      measurement: "Built-in timing"
    - metric: "User adoption"
      target: "50+ daily active users within 3 months"
      measurement: "Usage analytics"
  constraints:
    - type: usability
      description: "All commands must complete in under 1 second"
    - type: portability
      description: "Must run on Linux, macOS, and Windows"

capabilities:
  - id: capability.task_management
    description: Create, update, delete, and list tasks with metadata
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.project_organization
    description: Organize tasks into projects and categories
    priority: important

  - id: capability.task_search
    description: Search and filter tasks by various criteria
    priority: important

  - id: capability.data_export
    description: Export tasks to JSON, CSV, or Markdown formats
    priority: optional

components:
  - id: component.command_parser
    type: module
    responsibility: |
      Parse command-line arguments, validate input, and route commands
      to appropriate handlers. Supports subcommands and flags.
    technology: Rust with clap library
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.task_service
    type: module
    responsibility: |
      Manage task lifecycle including creation, updates, deletion, and queries.
      Enforce business rules and validation.
    technology: Rust
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.storage_layer
    type: module
    responsibility: |
      Persist task data to local filesystem with JSON-based storage.
      Handle file I/O, data serialization, and atomic writes.
    technology: Rust with serde for JSON
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.search_engine
    type: module
    responsibility: |
      Provide fast task search and filtering capabilities.
      Support multiple search criteria and patterns.
    technology: Rust
    complexity: small
    external: false

interfaces:
  - id: interface.cli_input
    protocol: Command Line Arguments
    connects: [user, component.command_parser]
    direction: input
    description: |
      Standard command-line input with subcommands and flags.
      Example: `todo add --priority high "Fix bug"`

  - id: interface.cli_output
    protocol: stdout/stderr
    connects: [component.command_parser, user]
    direction: output
    description: |
      Formatted output to terminal with colors and tables.
      Supports JSON output for programmatic use.

  - id: interface.storage_file
    protocol: File System (JSON)
    connects: [component.storage_layer, filesystem]
    direction: read_write
    description: |
      Local file storage in user's home directory.
      File: ~/.todo/tasks.json

  - id: interface.service_storage
    protocol: Internal Function Calls
    connects: [component.task_service, component.storage_layer]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Task service requests storage operations.

data:
  - id: data.task
    description: Individual task with metadata
    owner: component.task_service
    structure: |
      - task_id (UUID)
      - title
      - description (optional)
      - status (todo, in_progress, done)
      - priority (low, medium, high, urgent)
      - project (optional)
      - created_at
      - completed_at (nullable)
      - tags (list)
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "Indefinite"

  - id: data.project
    description: Project for grouping related tasks
    owner: component.task_service
    structure: |
      - project_id (UUID)
      - name
      - description (optional)
      - color (hex code)
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "Indefinite"

workflows:
  - id: workflow.create_task
    trigger: |
      User executes: `todo add [options] <title>`
    steps:
      - step: parse_command
        component: component.command_parser
        description: "Parse arguments and validate input"
        output: parsed_command

      - step: create_task_record
        component: component.task_service
        input: parsed_command
        description: "Create task with default values"
        output: task_record

      - step: persist_task
        component: component.storage_layer
        input: task_record
        description: "Save task to file atomically"
        output: persisted

      - step: display_confirmation
        component: component.command_parser
        input: task_record
        description: "Show created task to user"
        output: displayed
    completion_criteria: |
      Task created, persisted, and confirmation displayed
    error_handling:
      - condition: invalid_input
        action: display_error_and_exit
      - condition: storage_failure
        action: display_error_and_suggest_manual_recovery

  - id: workflow.list_tasks
    trigger: |
      User executes: `todo list [filter]`
    steps:
      - step: parse_command
        component: component.command_parser
        description: "Parse list command and filters"
        output: parsed_filters

      - step: load_tasks
        component: component.storage_layer
        description: "Load all tasks from storage"
        output: all_tasks

      - step: filter_tasks
        component: component.search_engine
        input: [all_tasks, parsed_filters]
        description: "Apply filters to task list"
        output: filtered_tasks

      - step: display_results
        component: component.command_parser
        input: filtered_tasks
        description: "Format and display task table"
        output: displayed
    completion_criteria: |
      Tasks loaded, filtered, and displayed
    error_handling:
      - condition: no_tasks_found
        action: display_empty_state_message
      - condition: storage_failure
        action: display_error_and_exit

  - id: workflow.complete_task
    trigger: |
      User executes: `todo done <task_id>`
    steps:
      - step: parse_command
        component: component.command_parser
        description: "Parse task ID"
        output: task_id

      - step: load_task
        component: component.storage_layer
        input: task_id
        description: "Load specific task"
        output: task_record

      - step: update_task_status
        component: component.task_service
        input: [task_record, "done"]
        description: "Mark task as completed"
        output: updated_task

      - step: persist_update
        component: component.storage_layer
        input: updated_task
        description: "Save updated task"
        output: persisted

      - step: display_confirmation
        component: component.command_parser
        input: updated_task
        description: "Show completion message"
        output: displayed
    completion_criteria: |
      Task marked as completed and persisted
    error_handling:
      - condition: task_not_found
        action: display_error_message
      - condition: already_completed
        action: display_info_message
---


25.1.3 Structural Description
The CLI Todo Manager demonstrates a straightforward, single-purpose system architecture suitable for command-line tools.

25.1.3.1 Component Interactions

Command Parser serves as the entry point, handling all user input and routing
Task Service contains business logic and enforces task rules
Storage Layer abstracts file I/O and data persistence
Search Engine provides filtering and search capabilities

The architecture follows a layered pattern with clear separation of concerns: - Input handling (Command Parser) - Business logic (Task Service) - Data access (Storage Layer) - Query logic (Search Engine)


25.1.3.2 Key Characteristics

Single Execution Context: Each command runs independently; no long-running process
State Persistence: State maintained via local file storage
Minimal Dependencies: No external services required
Composable Design: Can be used in shell pipelines via JSON output mode



25.1.3.3 Complexity Considerations
This is classified as a small CLI tool because: - 4 components with clear responsibilities - 4 interfaces (simple command-line I/O) - 2 data entities (tasks and projects) - 3 workflows (create, list, complete)
The blueprint could be expanded to medium complexity by adding: - Task dependencies and subtasks - Recurring tasks and reminders - Cloud sync capabilities - Plugin system for extensions

25.2 Example 2 — Web Application Blueprint

25.2.1 System Overview
The Blog Web Platform provides a complete solution for creating, managing, and publishing blog posts. It serves as a representative example of a typical web application with user authentication, content management, and public-facing content delivery.
Use Cases: - Authors create and publish blog posts with rich formatting - Readers browse and comment on posts - Administrators manage users and moderate content - Public RSS feed syndication
System Type: Web Application (Appendix B, Section 2) Complexity: medium


25.2.2 YAML Structure
---
blueprint:
  id: web.blog.platform.v1
  name: Blog Web Platform
  version: 1.0.0
  system_type: Web Application
  complexity: medium
  created_date: 2026-03-11
  authors: [Web Platform Team]

goal:
  description: |
    Provide a web platform for authors to create, manage, and publish blog posts,
    and for readers to discover and engage with content.
  success_metrics:
    - metric: "Page load time"
      target: "< 2s (p95)"
      measurement: "Real User Monitoring"
    - metric: "Concurrent users"
      target: "1000 concurrent users"
      measurement: "Load testing"
    - metric: "Content creation time"
      target: "< 5 minutes from login to publish"
      measurement: "User analytics"
  constraints:
    - type: performance
      description: "Support 10,000 page views per day"
    - type: compatibility
      description: "Support modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)"
    - type: regulatory
      description: "Comply with accessibility guidelines (WCAG 2.1)"

capabilities:
  - id: capability.user_authentication
    description: User registration, login, and session management
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.content_creation
    description: Create, edit, and publish blog posts with rich formatting
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.content_display
    description: Display published posts to public readers
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.comment_system
    description: Allow readers to comment on posts
    priority: important

  - id: capability.content_search
    description: Search posts by keywords and tags
    priority: important

  - id: capability.rss_feed
    description: Provide RSS feed for syndication
    priority: optional

components:
  - id: component.web_frontend
    type: frontend
    responsibility: |
      Provide responsive web interface for content creation and consumption.
      Handle client-side routing and state management.
    technology: React + TypeScript
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.api_service
    type: backend_service
    responsibility: |
      Expose REST API for frontend and serve public content.
      Handle authentication, authorization, and request processing.
    technology: Node.js + Express
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.database
    type: data_store
    responsibility: |
      Persist users, posts, comments, and related data.
      Provide transactional data integrity.
    technology: PostgreSQL
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.cache_layer
    type: data_store
    responsibility: |
      Cache frequently accessed content and session data
      to improve performance and reduce database load.
    technology: Redis
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.search_index
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Maintain search index for posts and enable fast search queries.
    technology: Elasticsearch
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.image_storage
    type: external_service
    responsibility: |
      Store and serve blog post images and media files.
    technology: AWS S3 or similar
    complexity: toy
    external: true

interfaces:
  - id: interface.http_api
    protocol: HTTP/REST
    connects: [component.web_frontend, component.api_service]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      REST API for all frontend operations.
      Uses JSON request/response format.
    authentication: jwt_token

  - id: interface.database_connection
    protocol: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol
    connects: [component.api_service, component.database]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Direct database connection for data persistence.
      Uses connection pooling.
    connection_pool_size: 20

  - id: interface.cache_operations
    protocol: Redis Protocol
    connects: [component.api_service, component.cache_layer]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Cache access for session data and cached content.
    ttl_default: 3600

  - id: interface.search_api
    protocol: HTTP
    connects: [component.api_service, component.search_index]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Search queries for post content and metadata.

  - id: interface.image_upload
    protocol: HTTPS/REST
    connects: [component.api_service, component.image_storage]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Upload and retrieve images from cloud storage.

  - id: interface.public_content
    protocol: HTTP
    connects: [component.api_service, public_readers]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Public API for reading published posts (no auth required).

data:
  - id: data.user
    description: User account information
    owner: component.api_service
    structure: |
      - user_id (UUID, primary key)
      - email (unique, indexed)
      - password_hash (bcrypt)
      - display_name
      - role (author, admin)
      - created_at
      - updated_at
    sensitivity: confidential
    retention: "365 days after account closure"

  - id: data.post
    description: Blog post with content and metadata
    owner: component.api_service
    structure: |
      - post_id (UUID, primary key)
      - author_id (foreign key)
      - title
      - slug (URL-friendly identifier)
      - content (Markdown)
      - html_content (rendered HTML)
      - status (draft, published, archived)
      - published_at (nullable)
      - created_at
      - updated_at
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "Indefinite"

  - id: data.comment
    description: User comments on posts
    owner: component.api_service
    structure: |
      - comment_id (UUID, primary key)
      - post_id (foreign key)
      - author_id (foreign key, nullable for anonymous)
      - content
      - status (pending, approved, rejected)
      - created_at
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "Indefinite"

  - id: data.session
    description: User session tokens
    owner: component.api_service
    structure: |
      - session_id (UUID, primary key)
      - user_id (foreign key)
      - token_hash
      - expires_at
    sensitivity: confidential
    retention: "24 hours (automatic expiration)"

workflows:
  - id: workflow.user_login
    trigger: |
      User submits login form with email and password
    steps:
      - step: authenticate_user
        component: component.api_service
        description: "Verify credentials and generate JWT token"
        output: session_token

      - step: cache_session
        component: component.api_service
        input: session_token
        description: "Cache session in Redis"
        output: cached

      - step: return_response
        component: component.api_service
        input: session_token
        description: "Return token to frontend"
        output: login_response
    completion_criteria: |
      Valid credentials produce session token, invalid produce 401
    error_handling:
      - condition: invalid_credentials
        action: return_401_unauthorized
      - condition: database_error
        action: return_500_internal_server_error

  - id: workflow.create_post
    trigger: |
      Author submits new blog post
    steps:
      - step: authenticate_request
        component: component.api_service
        description: "Verify JWT token and extract user context"
        output: user_context

      - step: validate_content
        component: component.api_service
        input: user_context
        description: "Validate post title and content"
        output: validated_post

      - step: save_post
        component: component.api_service
        input: validated_post
        description: "Create post record in database"
        output: post_record

      - step: render_markdown
        component: component.api_service
        input: post_record
        description: "Convert Markdown to HTML"
        output: rendered_content

      - step: update_post
        component: component.api_service
        input: [post_record, rendered_content]
        description: "Save rendered HTML to post"
        output: updated_post

      - step: return_response
        component: component.api_service
        input: updated_post
        description: "Return created post to frontend"
        output: post_response
    completion_criteria: |
      Post created, rendered, and returned to author
    error_handling:
      - condition: unauthorized
        action: return_401_unauthorized
      - condition: invalid_content
        action: return_400_bad_request

  - id: workflow.publish_post
    trigger: |
      Author changes post status from draft to published
    steps:
      - step: authenticate_request
        component: component.api_service
        description: "Verify author authorization"
        output: user_context

      - step: update_post_status
        component: component.api_service
        input: [post_id, "published"]
        description: "Update post status and set published_at timestamp"
        output: updated_post

      - step: invalidate_cache
        component: component.api_service
        input: post_id
        description: "Clear cached versions of this post"
        output: cache_cleared

      - step: index_post
        component: component.api_service
        input: updated_post
        description: "Add post to search index"
        output: indexed

      - step: return_response
        component: component.api_service
        input: updated_post
        description: "Return published post"
        output: post_response
    completion_criteria: |
      Post published, cache invalidated, and indexed
    error_handling:
      - condition: not_author
        action: return_403_forbidden
      - condition: post_not_found
        action: return_404_not_found

  - id: workflow.view_post
    trigger: |
      Reader requests published post by URL slug
    steps:
      - step: check_cache
        component: component.api_service
        description: "Check if post is cached"
        output: cached_post

      - step: load_from_database
        component: component.api_service
        input: slug
        description: "If not cached, load from database"
        output: post_record

      - step: cache_post
        component: component.api_service
        input: post_record
        description: "Cache post for future requests"
        output: cached

      - step: return_response
        component: component.api_service
        input: post_record
        description: "Return post to reader"
        output: post_response
    completion_criteria: |
      Post returned from cache or database
    error_handling:
      - condition: post_not_found
        action: return_404_not_found
      - condition: post_not_published
        action: return_403_forbidden
---


25.2.3 Structural Description
The Blog Web Platform demonstrates a classic three-tier web application architecture with additional infrastructure components for performance and search.

25.2.3.1 Component Interactions

Web Frontend: React-based SPA providing author and reader interfaces
API Service: Node.js backend handling authentication, content management, and public content delivery
Database: PostgreSQL for persistent storage of users, posts, and comments
Cache Layer: Redis for session management and content caching
Search Index: Elasticsearch for fast post search
Image Storage: External cloud storage for media files



25.2.3.2 Key Patterns

Layered Architecture: Frontend → API → Database with caching and search layers
JWT Authentication: Stateless authentication with token-based sessions
Content Caching: Published posts cached to reduce database load
Search Integration: External search index for fast queries
External Service Integration: Cloud storage for images and media



25.2.3.3 Complexity Considerations
This is classified as a medium web application because: - 6 components including external dependencies - 6 interfaces with multiple protocols (HTTP, database, cache, search) - 4 data entities with relationships - 4 workflows covering critical operations (login, create, publish, view)
The architecture could be expanded to large complexity by adding: - Multi-tenant support for multiple blogs - Advanced content features (tags, categories, media galleries) - Real-time collaboration for co-authoring - Advanced analytics and user engagement tracking - CDN integration for global content delivery

25.3 Example 3 — Data Pipeline Blueprint

25.3.1 System Overview
The Analytics ETL Pipeline processes raw event data from various sources, transforms it into structured analytics data, and aggregates it for reporting. This example demonstrates a data processing system with multiple stages and batch processing workflows.
Use Cases: - Ingest user activity events from web and mobile applications - Transform raw events into structured analytics records - Aggregate data for dashboards and reports - Provide data warehouse access for business intelligence
System Type: Data Pipeline (Appendix B, Section 5) Complexity: medium


25.3.2 YAML Structure
---
blueprint:
  id: pipeline.analytics.etl.v1
  name: Analytics ETL Pipeline
  version: 1.0.0
  system_type: Data Pipeline
  complexity: medium
  created_date: 2026-03-11
  authors: [Data Engineering Team]

goal:
  description: |
    Ingest, transform, and aggregate user activity data for analytics reporting
    and business intelligence. Provide reliable, timely data for dashboards.
  success_metrics:
    - metric: "Data freshness"
      target: "< 4 hours from event to dashboard"
      measurement: "Pipeline monitoring"
    - metric: "Processing throughput"
      target: "1M events per hour"
      measurement: "Pipeline metrics"
    - metric: "Data accuracy"
      target: "> 99.9% valid records"
      measurement: "Quality checks"
  constraints:
    - type: reliability
      description: "Must handle duplicate events idempotently"
    - type: performance
      description: "Must process daily data within 6-hour window"
    - type: regulatory
      description: "Must comply with data retention and privacy policies"

capabilities:
  - id: capability.data_ingestion
    description: Ingest events from web, mobile, and API sources
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.data_transformation
    description: Clean, validate, and transform raw events
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.data_aggregation
    description: Aggregate transformed data for analytics queries
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.quality_monitoring
    description: Monitor data quality and detect anomalies
    priority: important

  - id: capability.data_lineage
    description: Track data origin and transformation history
    priority: important

components:
  - id: component.ingestion_service
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Receive events from web/mobile clients and API sources.
      Buffer events and validate schema compliance.
    technology: Python + FastAPI
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.message_queue
    type: infrastructure
    responsibility: |
      Buffer events between ingestion and processing stages.
      Provide reliable message delivery and replay capabilities.
    technology: Apache Kafka
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.transformation_engine
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Process events from message queue, clean and transform data,
      handle deduplication and enrichment.
    technology: Apache Spark
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.quality_checker
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Validate transformed data for quality and completeness.
      Detect anomalies and trigger alerts for issues.
    technology: Python + Great Expectations
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.data_warehouse
    type: data_store
    responsibility: |
      Store processed and aggregated data for analytics queries.
      Provide SQL access for BI tools and dashboards.
    technology: Snowflake
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.metadata_store
    type: data_store
    responsibility: |
      Store pipeline metadata, data lineage, and quality metrics.
      Track pipeline runs and data versioning.
    technology: PostgreSQL
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.alerting_service
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Monitor pipeline health and send alerts for failures or quality issues.
    technology: Python + PagerDuty API
    complexity: small
    external: false

interfaces:
  - id: interface.event_ingestion_api
    protocol: HTTP/REST
    connects: [web_mobile_clients, component.ingestion_service]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      API for submitting events from web and mobile applications.
      Batch endpoint for bulk event submission.
    rate_limit: "10000 events/second"
    authentication: api_key

  - id: interface.kafka_producer
    protocol: Kafka
    connects: [component.ingestion_service, component.message_queue]
    direction: event_stream
    description: |
      Ingestion service publishes events to Kafka topics.
    topics: [raw_events.web, raw_events.mobile]

  - id: interface.kafka_consumer
    protocol: Kafka
    connects: [component.transformation_engine, component.message_queue]
    direction: event_stream
    description: |
      Transformation engine consumes events from Kafka topics.

  - id: interface.transformation_check
    protocol: Internal
    connects: [component.transformation_engine, component.quality_checker]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Transformation engine sends data for quality validation.

  - id: interface.warehouse_load
    protocol: Snowflake Connector
    connects: [component.transformation_engine, component.data_warehouse]
    direction: batch_write
    description: |
      Batch loading of transformed data into data warehouse tables.

  - id: interface.warehouse_query
    protocol: SQL
    connects: [bi_tools, component.data_warehouse]
    direction: query
    description: |
      SQL access for BI tools and dashboards.

  - id: interface.metadata_write
    protocol: PostgreSQL
    connects: [component.transformation_engine, component.metadata_store]
    direction: write
    description: |
      Write pipeline metadata and lineage information.

  - id: interface.alert_send
    protocol: HTTPS/Webhook
    connects: [component.alerting_service, pagerduty]
    direction: output
    description: |
      Send alerts to monitoring and on-call systems.

data:
  - id: data.raw_event
    description: Incoming user activity events
    owner: component.ingestion_service
    structure: |
      - event_id (UUID)
      - event_type (page_view, click, purchase, etc.)
      - user_id (nullable for anonymous)
      - timestamp
      - properties (JSON)
      - source (web, mobile, api)
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "90 days (raw), 7 years (aggregated)"

  - id: data.transformed_event
    description: Cleaned and validated events
    owner: component.transformation_engine
    structure: |
      - event_id (UUID)
      - event_type
      - user_id (normalized)
      - timestamp (normalized timezone)
      - properties (validated JSON)
      - processed_at
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "2 years"

  - id: data.aggregated_metrics
    description: Daily and hourly aggregated metrics
    owner: component.transformation_engine
    structure: |
      - metric_name
      - time_bucket
      - metric_value
      - dimensions (JSON)
      - calculated_at
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "7 years"

  - id: data.pipeline_metadata
    description: Pipeline run information and data lineage
    owner: component.metadata_store
    structure: |
      - run_id (UUID)
      - pipeline_name
      - start_time
      - end_time
      - status (running, completed, failed)
      - records_processed
      - error_details (JSON)
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "2 years"

workflows:
  - id: workflow.ingestion_pipeline
    trigger: |
      Web/mobile clients send events via API
    steps:
      - step: receive_event
        component: component.ingestion_service
        description: "Receive HTTP POST with event data"
        output: raw_event

      - step: validate_schema
        component: component.ingestion_service
        input: raw_event
        description: "Validate event structure and required fields"
        output: validated_event

      - step: publish_to_kafka
        component: component.ingestion_service
        input: validated_event
        description: "Publish event to appropriate Kafka topic"
        output: published

      - step: acknowledge_request
        component: component.ingestion_service
        description: "Return 202 Accepted to client"
        output: response
    completion_criteria: |
      Event received, validated, and published to Kafka
    error_handling:
      - condition: invalid_schema
        action: return_400_bad_request
      - condition: kafka_unavailable
        action: queue_locally_and_retry
      - condition: rate_limit_exceeded
        action: return_429_too_many_requests

  - id: workflow.transformation_pipeline
    trigger: |
      New events available in Kafka topics
    steps:
      - step: consume_events
        component: component.transformation_engine
        description: "Read batch of events from Kafka"
        output: event_batch

      - step: deduplicate_events
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: event_batch
        description: "Remove duplicate events based on event_id"
        output: deduplicated_batch

      - step: transform_events
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: deduplicated_batch
        description: "Clean, normalize, and enrich events"
        output: transformed_batch

      - step: check_quality
        component: component.quality_checker
        input: transformed_batch
        description: "Validate data quality and completeness"
        output: quality_report

      - step: handle_quality_issues
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: quality_report
        description: "Quarantine or reject invalid records"
        output: cleaned_batch

      - step: load_to_warehouse
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: cleaned_batch
        description: "Batch load transformed data into data warehouse"
        output: load_result

      - step: write_metadata
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: load_result
        description: "Record pipeline run metadata"
        output: metadata_saved

      - step: commit_offsets
        component: component.transformation_engine
        description: "Commit Kafka offsets to mark events as processed"
        output: committed
    completion_criteria: |
      Events transformed, quality-checked, and loaded to warehouse
    error_handling:
      - condition: quality_threshold_breached
        action: pause_pipeline_and_alert
      - condition: warehouse_unavailable
        action: retry_with_backoff_and_alert
      - condition: transformation_error
        action: log_error_and_skip_record

  - id: workflow.aggregation_pipeline
    trigger: |
      Scheduled job runs daily and hourly
    steps:
      - step: initiate_aggregation
        component: component.transformation_engine
        description: "Start scheduled aggregation job"
        output: job_id

      - step: read_transformed_data
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: job_id
        description: "Query transformed events for time bucket"
        output: event_data

      - step: calculate_metrics
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: event_data
        description: "Aggregate by dimensions and calculate metrics"
        output: aggregated_metrics

      - step: write_aggregations
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: aggregated_metrics
        description: "Write aggregated metrics to warehouse"
        output: write_result

      - step: update_metadata
        component: component.transformation_engine
        input: write_result
        description: "Record aggregation job metadata"
        output: metadata_updated
    completion_criteria: |
      Metrics calculated and written to warehouse
    error_handling:
      - condition: data_missing
        action: log_warning_and_continue
      - condition: aggregation_error
        action: retry_job_with_backoff

  - id: workflow.quality_monitoring
    trigger: |
      Continuous monitoring of pipeline health
    steps:
      - step: check_pipeline_status
        component: component.alerting_service
        description: "Query pipeline status from metadata store"
        output: status

      - step: check_quality_metrics
        component: component.alerting_service
        description: "Query quality metrics from recent runs"
        output: quality_metrics

      - step: evaluate_health
        component: component.alerting_service
        input: [status, quality_metrics]
        description: "Determine if pipeline is healthy"
        output: health_status

      - step: trigger_alert_if_needed
        component: component.alerting_service
        input: health_status
        description: "Send alert if issues detected"
        output: alert_sent
    completion_criteria: |
      Pipeline health evaluated and alerts sent if needed
    error_handling:
      - condition: pipeline_failed
        action: send_critical_alert
      - condition: quality_degraded
        action: send_warning_alert
---


25.3.3 Structural Description
The Analytics ETL Pipeline demonstrates a multi-stage data processing system with batch and streaming components.

25.3.3.1 Component Interactions

Ingestion Service: Receives events from clients and validates schema
Message Queue: Kafka buffers events between ingestion and processing
Transformation Engine: Spark processes, cleans, and transforms events
Quality Checker: Validates data quality and detects anomalies
Data Warehouse: Snowflake stores processed and aggregated data
Metadata Store: PostgreSQL tracks pipeline metadata and lineage
Alerting Service: Monitors health and sends alerts



25.3.3.2 Key Patterns

Event-Driven Architecture: Kafka enables decoupled event streaming
Batch Processing: Spark processes data in batches for efficiency
Quality Gates: Quality checker validates data before loading
Separation of Concerns: Ingestion, transformation, and aggregation are separate stages
Monitoring and Alerting: Continuous health monitoring with alerting



25.3.3.3 Complexity Considerations
This is classified as a medium data pipeline because: - 7 components including infrastructure services - 8 interfaces with multiple protocols (HTTP, Kafka, SQL, webhooks) - 4 data entities with different retention policies - 4 workflows covering ingestion, transformation, aggregation, and monitoring
The architecture could be expanded to large complexity by adding: - Real-time streaming with additional Kafka consumers - Machine learning model integration for anomaly detection - Multiple data sources with different schemas - Advanced data governance and privacy controls - Multi-region deployment for disaster recovery

title: 25  Appendix D — Example Blueprints (CLI / Web / Pipeline / Agent)
text:
25.4 Example 4 — Agent System Blueprint

25.4.1 System Overview
The Autonomous Task Agent is an AI-powered system capable of planning and executing complex tasks by interacting with external tools and APIs. This example demonstrates an agent-based architecture with planning, memory, and tool execution capabilities.
Use Cases: - Research tasks requiring information gathering from multiple sources - Document creation and formatting tasks - Data analysis and report generation - Multi-step workflows with decision points
System Type: Agent System (Appendix B, Section 6) Complexity: medium


25.4.2 YAML Structure
---
blueprint:
  id: agent.task.executor.v1
  name: Autonomous Task Agent
  version: 1.0.0
  system_type: Agent System
  complexity: medium
  created_date: 2026-03-11
  authors: [AI Agent Research Team]

goal:
  description: |
    Execute complex tasks by planning actions, making decisions, and interacting
    with external tools autonomously. Provide reliable task completion with
    transparency about the agent's reasoning and actions.
  success_metrics:
    - metric: "Task completion rate"
      target: "> 85% for defined task types"
      measurement: "Task tracking and evaluation"
    - metric: "Average task duration"
      target: "< 10 minutes for typical tasks"
      measurement: "Performance monitoring"
    - metric: "Tool usage accuracy"
      target: "> 95% correct tool selection"
      measurement: "Action logging and analysis"
  constraints:
    - type: safety
      description: "Must operate within defined tool boundaries"
    - type: transparency
      description: "Must log all decisions and actions for review"
    - type: reliability
      description: "Must handle tool failures gracefully with fallbacks"

capabilities:
  - id: capability.task_planning
    description: Decompose tasks into action plans with dependencies
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.tool_execution
    description: Invoke external tools and APIs to perform actions
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.memory_management
    description: Maintain context, history, and learned information
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.decision_making
    description: Make decisions at runtime based on context and observations
    priority: critical

  - id: capability.error_recovery
    description: Detect failures and implement recovery strategies
    priority: important

  - id: capability.explanation_generation
    description: Generate explanations of reasoning and actions
    priority: important

components:
  - id: component.planner
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Analyze task requirements and generate action plans.
      Break down complex tasks into subtasks with dependencies.
    technology: Python + LLM API
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.execution_engine
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Execute actions planned by the planner.
      Invoke tools via adapters and handle responses.
    technology: Python
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.memory_store
    type: data_store
    responsibility: |
      Maintain short-term context and long-term memory.
      Store task history, observations, and learned patterns.
    technology: Vector Database (e.g., Pinecone) + Redis
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.tool_adapter
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Provide standardized interfaces to external tools and APIs.
      Handle authentication, error handling, and response parsing.
    technology: Python
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.decision_engine
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Make runtime decisions based on context, observations, and planning.
      Evaluate alternatives and choose optimal actions.
    technology: Python + LLM API
    complexity: medium
    external: false

  - id: component.explainer
    type: service
    responsibility: |
      Generate human-readable explanations of agent reasoning and actions.
      Provide transparency and audit trail.
    technology: Python + LLM API
    complexity: small
    external: false

  - id: component.user_interface
    type: frontend
    responsibility: |
      Provide interface for users to submit tasks and monitor progress.
      Display agent decisions, actions, and explanations.
    technology: Web Interface (React)
    complexity: small
    external: false

interfaces:
  - id: interface.task_input
    protocol: HTTP/REST
    connects: [user, component.user_interface]
    direction: input
    description: |
      Users submit tasks through web interface.
    authentication: user_session

  - id: interface.planner_decision
    protocol: Internal API
    connects: [component.planner, component.execution_engine]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Planner provides action plans to execution engine.

  - id: interface.tool_invocation
    protocol: Internal API
    connects: [component.execution_engine, component.tool_adapter]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Execution engine requests tool invocations via adapters.

  - id: interface.memory_read_write
    protocol: Vector DB API + Redis
    connects: [component.planner, component.memory_store]
    direction: read_write
    description: |
      Planner reads context and writes observations to memory.

  - id: interface.decision_query
    protocol: Internal API
    connects: [component.execution_engine, component.decision_engine]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Execution engine queries decision engine for action choices.

  - id: interface.explanation_request
    protocol: Internal API
    connects: [component.execution_engine, component.explainer]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Execution engine requests explanations for actions.

  - id: interface.external_tool_api
    protocol: HTTP/gRPC (varies by tool)
    connects: [component.tool_adapter, external_tools]
    direction: request_response
    description: |
      Adapter invokes external tools and APIs.
    authentication: api_keys

  - id: interface.user_feedback
    protocol: WebSocket
    connects: [component.user_interface, user]
    direction: bidirectional
    description: |
      Real-time updates on agent progress and decisions.

data:
  - id: data.task_context
    description: Current task being executed and progress
    owner: component.memory_store
    structure: |
      - task_id (UUID)
      - task_description
      - current_step
      - plan (JSON)
      - progress_percentage
      - status (planning, executing, completed, failed)
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "90 days"

  - id: data.action_plan
    description: Planned sequence of actions to complete task
    owner: component.planner
    structure: |
      - plan_id (UUID)
      - task_id (foreign key)
      - steps (JSON array)
      - dependencies (JSON graph)
      - estimated_duration
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "90 days"

  - id: data.memory_record
    description: Observations, facts, and learned information
    owner: component.memory_store
    structure: |
      - record_id (UUID)
      - task_id (foreign key)
      - content (text)
      - embedding (vector)
      - timestamp
      - importance_score
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "1 year"

  - id: data.action_log
    description: History of all agent actions and decisions
    owner: component.execution_engine
    structure: |
      - action_id (UUID)
      - task_id (foreign key)
      - action_type
      - tool_used
      - parameters (JSON)
      - result (JSON)
      - reasoning (text)
      - timestamp
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "1 year"

  - id: data.explanation
    description: Human-readable explanations of agent behavior
    owner: component.explainer
    structure: |
      - explanation_id (UUID)
      - task_id (foreign key)
      - action_id (foreign key)
      - explanation_text
      - generated_at
    sensitivity: internal
    retention: "90 days"

workflows:
  - id: workflow.task_execution_cycle
    trigger: |
      User submits task through web interface
    steps:
      - step: receive_task
        component: component.user_interface
        description: "Receive task from user"
        output: task_request

      - step: initialize_context
        component: component.memory_store
        input: task_request
        description: "Create task context in memory"
        output: context_created

      - step: plan_actions
        component: component.planner
        input: context_created
        description: "Generate action plan to complete task"
        output: action_plan

      - step: save_plan
        component: component.memory_store
        input: action_plan
        description: "Store action plan in memory"
        output: plan_saved

      - step: begin_execution
        component: component.execution_engine
        input: plan_saved
        description: "Start executing action plan"
        output: execution_started

      - step: execute_next_action
        component: component.execution_engine
        description: "Execute next action in plan"
        output: action_result

      - step: record_observation
        component: component.memory_store
        input: action_result
        description: "Store observation from action"
        output: observation_recorded

      - step: evaluate_progress
        component: component.decision_engine
        input: [observation_recorded, action_plan]
        description: "Determine if plan needs adjustment"
        output: progress_evaluation

      - step: adjust_plan_if_needed
        component: component.planner
        input: progress_evaluation
        description: "Modify plan based on observations"
        output: updated_plan

      - step: generate_explanation
        component: component.explainer
        input: [action_result, progress_evaluation]
        description: "Generate explanation of action and reasoning"
        output: explanation

      - step: update_user
        component: component.user_interface
        input: explanation
        description: "Display progress to user"
        output: user_updated

      - step: check_completion
        component: component.execution_engine
        input: [progress_evaluation, action_plan]
        description: "Determine if task is complete"
        output: completion_status

      - step: complete_task
        component: component.execution_engine
        input: completion_status
        description: "Finalize task and mark as complete"
        output: task_completed
    completion_criteria: |
      All actions completed successfully or task marked as done
    error_handling:
      - condition: tool_failure
        action: retry_with_alternative_tool
      - condition: plan_failure
        action: regenerate_plan_and_retry
      - condition: max_retries_exceeded
        action: mark_task_failed_and_notify_user

  - id: workflow.tool_invocation
    trigger: |
      Execution engine needs to invoke a tool
    steps:
      - step: select_tool
        component: component.tool_adapter
        description: "Select appropriate tool for action"
        output: tool_selection

      - step: prepare_parameters
        component: component.tool_adapter
        input: [tool_selection, action_context]
        description: "Format parameters for tool API"
        output: prepared_parameters

      - step: invoke_tool
        component: component.tool_adapter
        input: prepared_parameters
        description: "Call external tool API"
        output: tool_response

      - step: parse_response
        component: component.tool_adapter
        input: tool_response
        description: "Parse and validate tool response"
        output: parsed_result

      - step: handle_errors
        component: component.tool_adapter
        input: parsed_result
        description: "Handle tool errors and retries"
        output: final_result
    completion_criteria: |
      Tool invoked successfully with valid response or error handled
    error_handling:
      - condition: api_error
        action: retry_with_backoff_3_attempts
      - condition: authentication_error
        action: refresh_credentials_and_retry
      - condition: rate_limit_error
        action: wait_and_retry

  - id: workflow.plan_regeneration
    trigger: |
      Current plan is not working or observations indicate new approach needed
    steps:
      - step: analyze_failure
        component: component.planner
        description: "Understand why current plan failed"
        output: failure_analysis

      - step: generate_alternative
        component: component.planner
        input: failure_analysis
        description: "Generate alternative action plan"
        output: alternative_plan

      - step: validate_alternative
        component: component.decision_engine
        input: alternative_plan
        description: "Evaluate if alternative plan is viable"
        output: validation_result

      - step: adopt_alternative
        component: component.execution_engine
        input: validation_result
        description: "Switch to alternative plan"
        output: plan_switched
    completion_criteria: |
      New plan generated and validated
    error_handling:
      - condition: no_viable_alternative
        action: mark_task_failed_and_request_human_help
---


25.4.3 Structural Description
The Autonomous Task Agent demonstrates an AI-powered system with planning, memory, and tool execution capabilities.

25.4.3.1 Component Interactions

Planner: Analyzes tasks and generates action plans using LLM
Execution Engine: Executes plans and coordinates tool invocations
Memory Store: Maintains context and history using vector database
Tool Adapter: Provides standardized interfaces to external tools
Decision Engine: Makes runtime decisions based on context
Explainer: Generates human-readable explanations
User Interface: Provides task submission and monitoring



25.4.3.2 Key Patterns

ReAct Pattern: Reason (plan) + Act (execute) iteration loop
Memory Architecture: Vector database for semantic search, Redis for fast access
Tool Abstraction: Standardized adapter pattern for diverse tools
Transparency: Explanation generation for all actions
Error Recovery: Multiple fallback strategies for tool failures



25.4.3.3 Complexity Considerations
This is classified as a medium agent system because: - 7 components including specialized AI services - 8 interfaces with internal and external protocols - 5 data entities with different storage mechanisms - 3 workflows covering execution, tool invocation, and plan regeneration
The architecture could be expanded to large complexity by adding: - Multi-agent coordination for parallel task execution - Hierarchical agent organization (master agent + specialist agents) - Advanced memory architectures with long-term learning - Tool marketplace with dynamic tool discovery - Human-in-the-loop workflows for approval and guidance

This consistency demonstrates the central idea of the blueprint framework:
Different systems may vary widely in implementation and scale, but their architectural structures can be represented using a shared blueprint model.


25.5.2 Key Insights

Universal Structure: Every system can be described using the same 6 kernel elements
Scalability: The framework works for simple CLI tools and complex agent systems
Composability: Consistent structure enables blueprint reuse and composition
Analysis: Shared structure enables cross-system pattern discovery and comparison
Automation: Uniform structure supports automated analysis and validation



25.5.3 Usage Guidance
When creating your own blueprints:

Start with the Kernel: Ensure all 6 sections are present
Reference Examples: Study similar system types for patterns
Adapt to Context: Adjust detail level based on complexity
Maintain Consistency: Use the same structure across all blueprints
Iterate and Refine: Blueprints evolve with system understanding

title: 26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)
text:
32.1 Composability
Definition: The quality of a blueprint that enables it to be combined with other blueprints without ambiguity. Composability requires clear interfaces, well-defined boundaries, and consistent data structures.
Context: Composability is a key quality attribute that enables blueprint reuse and system integration.
Usage Example: “The payment processing blueprint has high composability because it defines clear interfaces and data contracts for integration.”
Related Terms: - Composition: Process of combining composable blueprints - Interface: Contract enabling composition - Boundary: System edge for composition
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Assuming all blueprints are composable (composability must be designed) - ❌ Treating composition as simple concatenation (composition requires integration) - ❌ Ignoring interface compatibility (composability depends on well-defined interfaces)
Introduced In: Chapter 11
crumbs: Appendices
26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)

title: 26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)
text:
32.2 Feasibility
Definition: The quality of a blueprint describing a system that can be implemented realistically given technical, operational, and resource constraints.
Context: Feasibility ensures that blueprints represent achievable systems, not theoretical constructs.
Usage Example: “The blueprint review confirmed feasibility by verifying that all performance requirements were achievable with proposed architecture.”
Related Terms: - Constraint: Requirement affecting feasibility - Implementation: Realization testing feasibility - Technical Debt: Accumulated complexity affecting feasibility
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Assuming structural correctness implies feasibility (sound architecture may be infeasible) - ❌ Treating feasibility as binary (feasibility is a spectrum with risk levels) - ❌ Ignoring operational constraints (technical feasibility isn’t enough, must consider operations)
Introduced In: Chapter 16
crumbs: Appendices
26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)

title: 26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)
text:
32.3 Blueprint Discipline
Definition: The minimal set of practices and processes required to create and maintain high-quality blueprints. Discipline includes blueprint creation, review, version control, and integration with development workflows.
Context: Discipline ensures that blueprints remain useful, accurate, and consistent over time.
Usage Example: “The team adopted blueprint discipline including mandatory reviews, version control, and integration with the CI/CD pipeline.”
Related Terms: - Review: Quality validation process - Version Control: Tracking blueprint evolution - Workflow: Integration with development processes
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Treating discipline as optional (discipline is essential for quality) - ❌ Assuming discipline means bureaucracy (discipline can be lightweight and effective) - ❌ Focusing only on creation (discipline includes maintenance and evolution)
Introduced In: Chapter 17
crumbs: Appendices
26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)

title: 26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)
text:
33.1 System Type
Definition: A classification category based on the primary architectural purpose of a system. System types provide a taxonomy for organizing and searching blueprints.
Context: System types enable pattern discovery, retrieval, and comparison across similar systems.
Usage Example: “The task management system is classified as a Web Application because its primary purpose is providing a browser-based user interface.”
Related Terms: - Taxonomy: Classification system for system types - Appendix B: Complete system type taxonomy - Pattern: Common architectural approach for system type
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Classifying by technology instead of purpose (system types are architectural, not technological) - ❌ Assuming every system fits single type (systems can be hybrids with multiple characteristics) - ❌ Treating classification as rigid (classification is a tool, not a straitjacket)
Introduced In: Appendix B
crumbs: Appendices
26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)

title: 26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)
text:
33.2 Complexity
Definition: A classification of system scale based on component count, interface complexity, workflow complexity, and team requirements. Complexity levels are toy, small, medium, and large.
Context: Complexity classification guides blueprint detail level and architectural expectations.
Usage Example: “The system is classified as medium complexity because it has 12 components, 15 interfaces, and requires a 3-person team to maintain.”
Related Terms: - Component: Factor contributing to complexity - Interface: Factor contributing to complexity - Workflow: Factor contributing to complexity
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Confusing complexity with difficulty (complexity is scale, difficulty is subjective) - ❌ Assuming complexity is linear (complexity can grow non-linearly with additions) - ❌ Treating complexity as static (complexity can increase or decrease with changes)
Introduced In: Appendix B
crumbs: Appendices
26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)

title: 26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)
text:
33.3 Hybrid System
Definition: A system that combines characteristics from multiple system types. Hybrid systems have a primary type based on dominant purpose but also exhibit secondary characteristics from other types.
Context: Most real-world systems are hybrids. Proper classification acknowledges multi-type characteristics.
Usage Example: “The GitHub system is primarily a Web Application but also has Platform characteristics (APIs, services) and Data Pipeline characteristics (analytics processing).”
Related Terms: - Primary Type: Dominant system type - Secondary Characteristics: Features from other types - Tags: Labels indicating hybrid characteristics
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Forcing systems into single type (most systems are hybrids) - ❌ Ignoring secondary characteristics (secondary characteristics matter for search and analysis) - ❌ Treating hybrid as negative (hybrid is normal and expected)
Introduced In: Appendix B
crumbs: Appendices
26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)

title: 26  Appendix E — Glossary (Unified Terminology v0.1)
text:
34.1 Architecture View
Definition: A projection of the blueprint that focuses on structural relationships between system components. The architecture view emphasizes components, interfaces, dependencies, and structural boundaries.
Context: Architecture views are used by architects and engineers to understand system structure.
Usage Example: “The architecture view diagram shows the web frontend, API service, and database components with their REST and SQL interfaces.”
Related Terms: - Architecture: Structural aspect of blueprint - Component: Primary element in architecture view - Interface: Connection shown in architecture view
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Including behavioral details in architecture view (architecture view is structural) - ❌ Treating architecture view as complete blueprint (architecture view is one projection) - ❌ Assuming architecture view equals system design (design includes behavior, constraints, etc.)

34.2 Specification View
Definition: A projection of the blueprint that focuses on system behavior and expected outcomes. The specification view emphasizes capabilities, interface contracts, input/output behavior, and acceptance conditions.

Usage Example: “The specification view defines the user login capability including input validation, success responses, and error codes.”

Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Including implementation details in specification view (specification is behavioral, not implementation) - ❌ Treating specification view as test cases (specification defines behavior, tests verify it) - ❌ Assuming specification view is only for QA (specifications guide implementation and integration)

34.3 Operational View
Definition: A projection of the blueprint that focuses on runtime behavior and operational processes. The operational view emphasizes workflows, execution sequences, monitoring points, and operational procedures.
Context: Operational views are used by DevOps engineers, SREs, and operators to understand how the system runs.
Usage Example: “The operational view shows the request handling workflow including authentication, processing, and response generation steps.”
Related Terms: - Workflow: Primary element in operational view - Monitoring: Operational consideration in operational view - Procedure: Operational process described
Common Misinterpretations: - ❌ Including architectural details in operational view (operational view is behavioral, not structural) - ❌ Treating operational view as runbook (operational view describes behavior, runbooks provide procedures) - ❌ Assuming operational view is only for operators (operational view guides design for operations)

title: 27  Appendix F — Projection Map
text:
27.2 The Projection Concept

27.2.1 Definition
A projection is a derived representation of a blueprint that highlights a particular aspect of the system while maintaining consistency with the underlying model. Different projections serve different audiences and purposes.


27.2.2 Why Projections Matter
Problem: Traditional documentation creates multiple independent artifacts that drift apart over time.
Solution: Projections are always derived from the same blueprint, ensuring consistency.
Benefit: Teams get the right view for their needs without maintaining separate documents.


27.2.3 The Core Principle

The blueprint is the source of structural truth. All other artifacts are views derived from this central model.

This principle shifts architectural documentation from maintaining multiple documents to maintaining a single model and deriving specialized views.
crumbs: Appendices
27  Appendix F — Projection Map

title: 27  Appendix F — Projection Map
text:
27.3 The Projection Model

27.3.1 Conceptual Diagram
                    Blueprint (Core System Model)
                                │
                ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                │               │               │
                ▼               ▼               ▼
         Architecture View  Spec View  Operational View
         (Structure)       (Behavior)     (Runtime)
                │               │               │
                └───────────────┼───────────────┘
                                │
                                ▼
                    Consistency Guaranteed


27.3.2 Projection Hierarchy

Source Model: Blueprint (kernel + extensions)
Primary Projections: Architecture, Specification, Operational
Derived Views: Specialized views for specific audiences (e.g., security, performance)
Artifacts: Concrete deliverables (diagrams, docs, configs)



27.3.3 Key Characteristics
All projections share these characteristics:

Derived: Generated from blueprint, not created independently
Consistent: Always aligned with underlying blueprint
Focused: Emphasize specific aspects of the system
Audience-Specific: Tailored to particular stakeholders
Traceable: Can be traced back to blueprint elements

title: 27  Appendix F — Projection Map
text:
27.4 Architecture View

27.4.1 Definition
The Architecture View focuses on the structural relationships between system components. It answers “How is the system structured?”


27.4.2 Primary Audience

Software Architects: Design system structure
Technical Leads: Understand component relationships
Engineers: Navigate code organization
System Integrators: Plan integration points



27.4.3 What It Emphasizes

Components and their responsibilities
Interfaces and communication boundaries
Dependencies and coupling
Structural boundaries (internal vs external)
Technology choices (at architectural level)



27.4.4 Typical Representations

Component Diagrams: Boxes and arrows showing components and interfaces
Service Dependency Graphs: Dependency relationships between services
System Topology Diagrams: Physical or logical deployment structure
Layer Diagrams: Architectural layers and their relationships



27.4.5 Example Architecture View
┌─────────────┐         HTTP/REST          ┌─────────────┐
│   Web       │ ─────────────────────────► │   API       │
│  Frontend   │ ◄───────────────────────── │  Service    │
└─────────────┘    Session Tokens          └─────────────┘
                                               │
                                               │ PostgreSQL
                                               ▼
                                       ┌─────────────┐
                                       │  Database   │
                                       └─────────────┘

Key Elements Shown:
- Components (Frontend, API Service, Database)
- Interfaces (HTTP/REST, PostgreSQL)
- Communication patterns (request/response)
- Technology choices (implied by interface types)


27.4.6 Architecture View Content
Based on blueprint elements:



Blueprint Element
Architecture View Representation




Components
Nodes/boxes in diagram


Interfaces
Arrows/lines between nodes


Interface Protocols
Labels on arrows (HTTP, gRPC, etc.)


Component Responsibilities
Annotations or detailed diagrams


External Components
Distinct visual representation


System Boundaries
Enclosing boxes or zones





27.4.7 Generation Method

Extract Components: Read components: section from blueprint
Extract Interfaces: Read interfaces: section
Build Graph: Create nodes for components, edges for interfaces
Apply Layout: Arrange components logically (layered, hierarchical, etc.)
Add Labels: Annotate with protocols, responsibilities, technology
Format Output: Generate diagram (Mermaid, PlantUML, etc.)



27.4.8 Architecture View Checklist
When generating or reviewing architecture views:

All components from blueprint are represented
All interfaces are shown with protocols
Component responsibilities are clear
External components are distinguished
Communication patterns are evident
System boundaries are marked
Technology choices are indicated (if relevant)
Diagram is readable and well-organized



27.4.9 Common Pitfalls
❌ Including Behavioral Details: Architecture views should show structure, not workflows or behavior ❌ Implementation-Level Detail: Architecture is at component level, not class or function level ❌ Missing Interfaces: All communication should have defined interfaces ❌ Confusing Layout with Structure: Diagram layout doesn’t equal architectural structure

title: 27  Appendix F — Projection Map
text:
27.5 Specification View

27.5.1 Definition
The Specification View focuses on system behavior and expected outcomes. It answers “What should the system do and how should it behave?”


27.5.2 Primary Audience

Product Managers: Define requirements and acceptance criteria
QA Engineers: Create test cases and verify behavior
API Consumers: Integrate with system APIs
Business Stakeholders: Understand system capabilities



27.5.3 What It Emphasizes

Capabilities and their descriptions
Interface contracts (API specs, message formats)
Input/output behavior
Acceptance criteria and success conditions
Error conditions and responses
Performance and reliability requirements



27.5.4 Typical Representations

API Specifications: OpenAPI/Swagger documents
Functional Requirements: User stories and acceptance criteria
Behavior Specifications: State machines, decision tables
Contract Documents: SLAs, SLOs, performance guarantees



27.5.5 Example Specification View
# API Specification: User Authentication

capability: user_authentication

endpoints:
  /auth/login:
    method: POST
    description: Authenticate user and return session token
    request:
      email: string (required)
      password: string (required)
    response:
      success:
        status: 200
        body:
          token: string (JWT)
          user_id: string (UUID)
          expires_at: timestamp
      errors:
        401: Invalid credentials
        400: Invalid input
        429: Rate limit exceeded

  /auth/logout:
    method: POST
    description: Invalidate session token
    request:
      token: string (JWT, header)
    response:
      success:
        status: 200
        body:
          message: "Logged out successfully"
      errors:
        401: Invalid or expired token

acceptance_criteria:
  - Valid credentials return JWT token
  - Invalid credentials return 401
  - Token expires after 24 hours
  - Rate limit: 10 requests per minute per IP


27.5.6 Specification View Content
Based on blueprint elements:



Blueprint Element
Specification View Representation




Goal
Functional objectives and success metrics


Capabilities
Functional requirements and user stories


Interfaces
API contracts, message formats, protocols


Workflows
Behavioral sequences and state transitions


Success Metrics
Acceptance criteria and performance targets


Constraints
Non-functional requirements and limitations





27.5.7 Generation Method

Extract Capabilities: Read capabilities: section from blueprint
Extract Interface Contracts: Read interfaces: with protocols and formats
Extract Workflows: Read workflows: for behavior description
Extract Success Criteria: Read goal.success_metrics: and workflow completion criteria
Extract Constraints: Read goal.constraints: and any additional constraints
Format Output: Generate specification document (OpenAPI, requirements doc, etc.)



27.5.8 Specification View Checklist
When generating or reviewing specification views:

All capabilities are specified with clear behavior
Interface contracts include protocols, formats, and error conditions
Workflows describe expected behavior sequences
Acceptance criteria are measurable and testable
Performance requirements are specified (if applicable)
Error conditions are documented
Authentication and authorization requirements are specified
Constraints and limitations are documented



27.5.9 Common Pitfalls
❌ Including Implementation Details: Specifications define behavior, not how it’s implemented ❌ Vague Requirements: Specifications should be testable and unambiguous ❌ Missing Error Cases: Specifications must define behavior for error conditions ❌ Ignoring Edge Cases: Specifications should cover boundary conditions and unusual inputs
